title: The residual stream and the logit lens
summary: A shared workspace every layer adds to, and when the prediction forms.

steps.text: The pipeline map on the left draws the [[residual stream]]: the vertical line with ⊕ nodes is the vector each position carries. Each block's attention and MLP branch off it, compute, and add their result back at a ⊕. Every sublayer **reads** the stream and **adds** to it; nothing overwrites it. This view follows one position's vector (the last token, “She”) through every [[snapshot]]: each row is the stream at one point, from the embedding x₀ down to after the last MLP, and each column is one of its dimensions.
steps.prompt: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She

steps.text: Note that **what each sublayer writes** is now selected above the heatmap. Instead of the stream itself, each row now shows what one sublayer **added** to it (its Δ), with x₀ on top. Added together, the rows give the last snapshot from the previous step. Scroll down to the **Write size at position** bars to see how big each addition is: the thick bar is the size of what the sublayer wrote (‖Δ‖), the thin bar is the size of the stream after adding it (‖x‖). Long thick bars mark the sublayers that changed this position the most.

The **[[logit lens]]** asks what the model would predict if it stopped early. It takes each snapshot and decodes it as if it were the output of the last layer, using the final [[layer norm]] and the [[unembedding|unembedding W_U]], into a guess for the **next token**. Each column is a position in the prompt, and each row is one snapshot, from x₀ at the top to the model's real output at the bottom. A cell shows that row's top guess for the token that comes after the column's word; underlined cells are guesses that match the actual next token, shown in the **actual next** row.
Reading down a column shows the guess forming: often wrong early, right late. The right-hand column gives each row's accuracy.

ask.question: Click a cell in a column where an **early** row is already correct (underlined).
ask.correct: Some predictions are easy enough to be readable from the embeddings; others only form in the last layers.
ask.hint: Look in the top half of the rows for an underlined cell.
